messages:
Alex W.: quick heads-up — I ran into an odd case with our current pin metadata when migrating a Dedicated pool to Private. soft pins fell back to an unexpected model in prod :worried:
Maria T.: can you paste the pin blob you used?
Alex W.: sure — short excerpt:
```
pinned_models:
  - name: my-company/chat
    tag: \"v4.2\"
    strategy: \"soft\"  # try pinned, else fallback to compatible-alias
compatibility:
  allow_major_mismatch: false
```
Jamal R.: ugh that highlights the id problem. tag vs immutable digest. tags are user-friendly but not audit-safe. we should require an immutable ref for the audit log and allow a human alias separately.
Sophie L.: there’s also a namespace collision risk — customers can pin models like `acme/my-model` that might overlap with platform-curated catalog entries. we need a clear resolution rule (customer-first? catalog namespaced?).
Kevin H.: proposal (minimal): pins = list of {scope, model_ref, matcher, fallback_policy, created_by}. model_ref can be either `name:tag` or `name@sha256:...`. fallback_policy enum = [fail, regional_fallback, alias_fallback, best_compatible]. example:
```json
{"pins":[{"scope":"route","model_ref":"acme/reply@sha256:abcd1234","matcher":"exact","fallback_policy":"fail","created_by":"alex.w"}]}
```
infra-bot: schema-lint: pins.schema: ERROR at /pins/0 - missing required property `created_by` (fix in staging before merge)
Maria T.: we should add a `pin_intent` field to capture whether the pin is for correctness (strict) or cost/perf (soft). and a `fallback_priority` list so we can encode: [same-variant, same-model-different-quant, nearest-region].
Alex W.: +1. also thinking we need explicit scope options: route, tenant, org, region. make regional pins possible so ops can pin a region to a specific hardware-optimized variant.
Sophie L.: question: if a tenant pins `my-model@sha256:a` but we have alias `stable/my-model -> sha256:b` in catalog, what should happen when the tenant requests auto-updates? do we follow alias or respect immutable?
Jamal R.: rule suggestion: immutable refs always win for serving (for repeatability). alias updates allowed only when `pin_intent` != strict and the pin includes `allow_alias_updates: true`. otherwise alias changes should surface in console but not affect pinned traffic.
Kevin H.: implementation note: in rollout controller, store both `model_ref` and resolved `digest` with resolution metadata: {resolved_from_alias, resolved_at, resolver}. makes audits easier. We should also record the ancestry chain when an alias maps to a digest.
Maria T.: can we have a compact example of proposed full metadata? here’s a draft:
```json
{
  \"pins\": [
    {
      \"scope\": \"route\",
      \"region\": \"eu-west-1\",
      \"model_ref\": \"acme/reply:v4.2\",
      \"resolved_digest\": \"sha256:abcd...\",
      \"pin_intent\": \"soft\",
      \"allow_alias_updates\": false,
      \"fallback_priority\": [\"same-model-diff-quant\",\"nearest-region\"],
      \"created_by\": \"maria.t\",
      \"created_at\": \"2026-02-12T18:12:00Z\"
    }
  ],
  \"rollout\": {\"strategy\":\"canary\",\"canary_pct\":10,\"window_minutes\":30}
}
```
Sophie L.: thanks — that covers a lot. we need to bake in validation rules: region must match deployment region when scope=region; resolved_digest must be present for strict pins; created_by is mandatory.
Alex W.: ops ask — can we surface a human-readable explanation in the Console when a fallback occurs (e.g., \"pinned digest missing in region; fell back to alias stable/my-model\")? that will save pager noise.
Jamal R.: +1. also add a `fallback_reason` field to audit events so the console can show it and automated alerts can group by reason.
Maria T.: action items: 1) update schema draft with fields above, 2) add resolver metadata to audit logs, 3) run compatibility lint job across dedicated/private repos, 4) RFC PR early next week.
Kevin H.: I’ll start a linter rule and a small schema PR (will reference this thread).
Alex W.: thanks — I’ll open an issues list with reproducer and add a recording of the failure mode. tagging @SRE to watch for regressed fallback noise. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-check: schema-pr-rollback-safe — PASSED (staging)
Sophie L.: sounds good. leaving notes for RFC: include examples for tenant vs catalog name resolution, and a migration path for existing tag-only pins.
Alex W.: cool — closing this thread for now, will ping when RFC is up. (reaction :white_check_mark:)
